story_type: missing skiff found by search plane after days at sea
hook: Three men, one small skiff, four days lost in the Pacific.
narration: Three men had been missing in this sixteen foot skiff for four days.
They were about a hundred and ten miles southwest of Tarawa, in the Pacific nation of Kiribati.
One of them was twenty. The other two were fifty-five.
On October fifth, a Coast Guard Hercules from Air Station Barbers Point, Hawaii, found them.
A Hercules can search huge stretches of ocean, but it cannot land on water, so crews call the nearest ships for help.
[short pause] A South Korean fishing vessel, the Universe Kim, answered and turned toward them.
Its crew brought all three aboard, then lifted their skiff up with a crane.
outcome: All three mariners were reported in good condition, with no injuries.
title: Lost 4 days in a 16 foot skiff
description:
On Oct. 5, 2012, a Coast Guard HC-130 crew from Air Station Barbers Point found three mariners missing since Oct. 1 in a 16-foot skiff about 110 miles southwest of Tarawa, Kiribati. The fishing vessel Universe Kim picked them up.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video, Air Station Barbers Point, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/317769

facts.claim: HC-130 from Barbers Point found the skiff Oct. 5, 110 miles SW of Tarawa
facts.source_quote: A Coast Guard HC-130 Hercules aircraft crew from Air Station Barbers Point locates the crew of a 16 foot skiff Oct. 5, 2012, approximately 110 miles southwest of Tarawa, the Republic of Kiribati.

facts.claim: Three men, ages 20, 55, 55, missing since Oct. 1
facts.source_quote: The three-man crew, a 20-year-old and two 55-year-olds, had been missing and overdue since Oct. 1, 2012.

facts.claim: Aircrew requested a Good Samaritan vessel
facts.source_quote: The Coast Guard aircrew requested a Good Samaritan vessel assist with picking up the three mariners.

facts.claim: Universe Kim took them aboard and craned the skiff
facts.source_quote: The crew of the Universe Kim transferred the crewmembers aboard their vessel. They also picked up their 16-foot skiff with a crane and brought it aboard.
The three mariners were reported to be in good condition and with no injuries.
